visuals.title: lecture → LLM finetuning approaches
visuals.extracted_text: Finetuning: Adapting a pretrained model to a specific task by training the model on additional data
visuals.diagram_summary: Three-stage LLM finetuning pipeline: Stage 1 shows data preprocessing and attention mechanisms leading to building an LLM; Stage 2 shows pretraining and foundation model development with finetuning; Stage 3 shows classification and personal assistant applications with instruction dataset.

With pre-training, we saw that we are getting good results and when we give an input text, we are getting output which makes a lot of sense and it's pretty awesome.

So first, you might be thinking that, okay, we already pre-trained the Large Language Model and it seems to already work pretty well, right?
So then does that mean we have finished building our LLM? No.
Let me explain to you why do we need fine-tuning.
So let's say if you have pre-trained the model, that's fine, but what if you have a specific task?

Let's say if you want to make a chatbot as an airline using your data.
Essentially, if you want to make a specific chatbot, you can make a chatbot based on your data.
But if you want to make a specific application, the pre-trained model is not enough because it's pre-trained on general data available from all over the internet.
You need to train the model again on additional data.
This is called as fine-tuning.
So the formal definition of fine-tuning is adapting a pre-trained model to a specific task by training the model again on fine-tuned, on additional data.
There are some things which are very important here, some terminologies.
The first terminology is this specific task.
So fine-tuning is needed when you have certain specific tasks which need to be performed.
